system:
Two claims about the same repository contradict each other. Determine which is true.

You are working in the repository these claims are about. Read it before you answer — check whether
the configuration actually changed, and when. Do not adjudicate from the two claims alone when the
files and the history are there to settle it.

Possible outcomes:

new_wins        The new claim is correct; the existing one is stale. Something changed.
existing_wins   The existing claim still holds; the new one is mistaken or describes a special case.
both_scoped     Both are true under narrower scopes. Return the corrected scope for each.
                This is common — different environments, access paths, or time periods.
undecidable     The evidence does not settle it.

undecidable is a legitimate answer, not a failure. A human will decide. Choosing it costs a review;
guessing wrong silently corrupts the knowledge base. Prefer undecidable when genuinely uncertain.

Cite what you checked. If you read a file or a commit, say which and what it showed.

Do not modify anything. Answering this is a read; whatever else you can do here, this is not the
place to do it.

value.reasoning:
I couldn't check the repository. The only tool available here is StructuredOutput, so I had no way to read files or git history. That means I couldn't confirm whether the code uses transformers.js or calls a hosted embedding API, or when that changed.

The two claims directly contradict each other:
- The existing claim (first seen 2026-08-31) says local transformers.js embeddings were chosen, for privacy and consent reasons.
- The new claim says the choice was deliberately left undecided. Its evidence is a direct statement asking that it stay visibly unresolved rather than be quietly picked.

The new statement could mean the decision was reopened after 2026-08-31, which would make it the winner. It could also mean the original record overstated how settled the decision was. Or the code could use local embeddings today while the policy question is still open, which would make both claims true in narrower scopes. Without the repo and its history I can't tell these apart. The person asked for this to stay visible as undecided, so a human should decide rather than me guessing.
evidenceChecked: The text and evidence of both claims only. I couldn't read files or commits because no repository-reading tool was available.
